issues.display_title: Issue #1043: fix(map): the panorama route vanishes in Overview once a project also has drawn geometry (#1033)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1043-overview-route.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #1033. On /v/H2s94H3V (Pelee Island Blue Line (Demo)) the panorama route disappears as soon as the viewer zooms out past the Overview threshold — the same symptom #976 fixed and shipped in c2e4055.

Measured on the live link

.playwright-mcp/demo/1033/probe-overview.mjs, prod, label-canvas painted pixels:

Zoom Painted Marker buttons Toolbar
16.68 (landing) 1948 px 141 Search Area · Direction · Event · Floor 1
16.5 drawn 1074 the same
16.0 0 7 Search Area only
15.0 / 13.0 0 7 Search Area only

With no Building record there is no dropdown back to a building either, so below zoom 16.25 the visitor gets a blank basemap.

Root cause

#976 stopped Overview from engaging on a project with no massing to draw:

// src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts:114
const hasMassing = useMemo(
  () => (canvasData?.levels ?? []).some((level) => levelBBox(level) !== null),
  [canvasData],
);
const active = enabled && hasMassing;

The live project is no longer wall-less. Its level now carries 1 area and 4 walls — a rectangle roughly 848 × 781 m, createdAt 2026-09-16T04:31:16Z, four minutes before #1033 was filed (the same box as #1034). levelBBox is non-null, so hasMassing is true, Overview engages again, and PreviewOverlay.tsx:891 passes indoorHidden: outdoor into the label canvas, whose draw returns before anything indoor is painted:

// src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts:237
if (indoorHiddenRef.current) { markerHitsRef.current = []; ...; return; }

The connection lines (4,671 panoLinks) are drawn on that canvas, so they go with the markers and labels.

The guard is all-or-nothing per project: one drawn room re-hides an island-wide route. The pin markers are a separate, correct gate — siteScaleOnly={zoomedOut} (PreviewOverlay.tsx:1169) drops point-like anchors past the threshold regardless of Overview, and that stays (keeping 4,696 pin buttons on screen at island scale dropped panning to ~2 fps, #976).

Decisions (answered by PM on #1033)

  1. The line stays in Overview only when the route reaches beyond the buildings. An indoor tour's links stay hidden there — at Overview zoom they would draw as a mesh over the building shells (the Kuwait sample carries 2,097 panoramas).
  2. Pins stay hidden in Overview; the line alone carries the route. Unchanged from #976, which measured ~2 fps panning with all 4,696 pin buttons mounted at island scale.

Scope

  1. Decide per project whether the route is site-scale — compare the resolved connection bounds against the massing bounds (levelBBox per level, src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:208; connections resolve in src/lib/map/panoConnections.ts). A route that extends beyond the massing is outdoor content and survives Overview.
  2. Let the connection lines through the Overview gate — useFloorPlanLabels currently treats indoorHidden as "draw nothing indoor". Connection lines need to be drawn before that return when (1) holds, with markers, labels, route and dots still suppressed.
  3. Pass the flag from PreviewOverlay next to the existing connectionLines / indoorHidden props (PreviewOverlay.tsx:891, :913).
  4. Leave the #976 hasMassing guard alone — a project with no geometry at all must still never enter Overview; this task only covers the mixed case.
  5. Keep the connection-toggle button honest — with "Show connections" off (showConnections, PreviewOverlay.tsx:852) nothing is drawn in Overview either.

Acceptance criteria

  • On a project that has both a panorama route and drawn geometry, zooming out past the Overview threshold keeps the route's blue line on screen.
  • The route's pins, room labels and indoor floor detail stay hidden in Overview, as today.
  • Building massing still draws in Overview, and a project whose links all sit inside its buildings draws no links there (per the PM decision).
  • A project with no wall/area geometry behaves exactly as #976 shipped it — Overview never engages.
  • Turning "Show connections" off hides the line everywhere, Overview included.
  • Panning at site scale in Overview holds frame time at the #976 level (no per-pin work reintroduced).
  • Verified on /v/H2s94H3V with the GPU probe, not only in unit tests.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit all green.

RESULT

Fix

8f74ce5 fix(map): keep a panorama route on screen in Overview when it leaves the buildings — PR #1044

Root cause. #976 kept /v/H2s94H3V's route visible by never engaging Overview on a project with no wall or area geometry. One rectangle drawn on it (4 walls + 1 area) made hasMassing true, Overview engaged again below zoom 16.25, and the label canvas (useFloorPlanLabels) returned before drawing anything once indoorHidden was set — so the route's 4,671 links went with the markers and labels.

Per the PM on #1033 (1b, pins stay hidden):

  • connectionsLeaveBuildings (src/lib/map/panoConnections.ts) — true when a link has an end outside every building's bounds (per building, so the gap between two buildings is outside), grown by a 25 m margin so an entrance panorama just outside the door does not count.
  • PreviewOverlay passes connectionLines in Overview only when that holds; Show connections still wins.
  • useFloorPlanLabels strokes the connection lines ahead of the indoorHidden gate. Pins, labels, route and dots stay hidden in Overview. The stroke now sits under the canvas markers, as in the 2D editor.

The #976 guard is unchanged (no geometry → never Overview). No new dependency, no Go API change.

Verification

pnpm test 270 files / 2,470 passed, pnpm lint and tsc --noEmit clean. New tests in panoConnections.test.ts, useFloorPlanLabels.overview.test.tsx, PreviewOverlay.overviewConnections.test.tsx; the hook and overlay tests fail on development exactly at the regression.

GPU Chrome on /v/H2s94H3V, label-canvas pixels at zoom 16 / 15 / 13: development 0 / 0 / 0 → this branch 2,642 / 8,528 / 13,904, with 0 pin buttons mounted. Island pan 16.7 ms median, 0 long tasks on both builds (headless GPU). Close in on the route both builds paint the same 2,941 px.

Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1043/video-1043-overview-route.mp4 (before/after on the share link, HUD with pixels, pins and mode, toggle off/on, same pan on both halves — rig numbers p90 33.1 → 38.4 ms).

Not verified live: an indoor tour's links staying hidden in Overview (unit tests only — no published project with links inside a building).

issues.display_title: Issue #1048: feat(map): Panorama Link placement scope with a ghosted map (#1046 part 1)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1048-scope-ghost.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1046 (Panorama Link Mode Selection), part 1 of 3. The PM's answers to the clarifying questions on #1046 are folded into the rules below.

Context

  • Placement Scope today (src/lib/map/placement.ts): All Buildings, Selected Building, Selected Floor. #591 R23/R38 fixed it at three; for #1046 the PM decided to add Panorama Link as a fourth.
  • Every placement tool branches on the scope: "floor" writes the level frame, "allBuildings" the project frame, and anything else the building frame. This covers rotate/scale/nudge/reset in src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx and the Drag tool via useBuildingDrag in src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:312-316. A fourth value falls into the Selected Building branch, so without a guard Drag and the transform popup would move a whole building while the user believes they are working on panoramas.
  • A panorama on the map is a level.points entry whose infoId points at an Information record with pano. The links (canvasData.panoLinks) are drawn from those points' positions (src/lib/map/panoConnections.ts).

Scope

  1. Add Panorama Link to PlacementScope and to the scope menu (src/components/editor/toolbar/MapScopeButton.tsx). It uses the lucide Waypoints icon, the one the preview's "Show connections" button uses (PM).

  2. Selecting it turns Panorama Link mode on in the editor Map tab. Choosing another scope, or leaving the Map tab, turns it off.

  3. While the mode is on, these render ghosted (PM):

    • the active floor's rooms and walls
    • the other visible floors
    • the neighbouring building shells
    • every non-panorama object marker and label (areas, points, doors, shapes, safety)

    Panorama pins and their connection lines stay at full strength.

  4. Leaving the mode restores the normal appearance exactly.

  5. Until the group tools exist (part 3), the whole-layer placement tools do nothing in this scope: Drag and the transform popup's rotate / scale / nudge / reset must not change any project, building or floor frame.

Out of scope

  • Selecting panoramas (part 2) and transforming them (part 3).
  • The preview/live viewer and the Editor tab.

Acceptance criteria

  • The scope menu lists Panorama Link with the Waypoints icon. The move hint, the Drag tooltip and the transform popup tooltips all name it.
  • With Panorama Link selected, all four things listed in Scope 3 render ghosted, while panorama pins and links do not.
  • Switching to any other scope, or leaving the Map tab, restores the normal appearance.
  • No project, building or floor frame changes while the scope is Panorama Link, whichever of Drag / rotate / scale / nudge / reset is used. Covered by a unit test.
  • The three existing scopes behave as before.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; checked in the browser on a scratch copy of a panorama project.

RESULT

Released to development.

src/lib/map/ghost.ts scales each layer's own spec opacity, so leaving the mode writes the spec values back exactly; it re-applies on styledata while on (the owning hooks add their layers asynchronously and re-add them after a style swap) and never touches a map that was never ghosted. Ghost covers the floor plan model (active + other visible floors), the neighbouring building shells, the canvas labels and every non-panorama marker; a panorama is a point whose Information carries a tour pano, whatever label type it wears.

Guards until the group tools land (#1050): Drag and Edit placement are disabled in this scope, their handlers return early, picking the scope ends move mode, an open placement popup closes, and the mode ends with the Map tab.

Tests: src/lib/map/__tests__/ghost.test.ts, src/components/editor/__tests__/panoramaLinkScope.test.tsx, src/components/editor/map-markers/__tests__/MapObjectMarkers.panoramaLink.test.tsx. Mutation-checked. pnpm test / pnpm lint / tsc --noEmit green.

Browser check on the GPU, scratch copy of a panorama project: wall opacity 1 → 0.3 and back, 1,018 panorama chips un-ghosted while the non-panorama marker is ghosted, Drag/Edit placement disabled then re-enabled, Map-tab round trip back on Selected Building.

Commit: 2e93885 · PR #1051 -> development (f829e31)

Demo (48 s): .playwright-mcp/demo/1048/video-1048-scope-ghost.mp4 — the scope, the ghost, the locked frame tools, and the map coming back. Part of the feature-wide one in .playwright-mcp/demo/1046/.

Released to main: PR #1054 (9faeb19).

issues.display_title: Issue #1049: feat(map): Shift-select panoramas in Panorama Link mode — click and box selection with one outline (#1046 part 2)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1049-shift-select.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1046 (Panorama Link Mode Selection), part 2 of 3. Builds on #1048.

Context

  • useMapSelect (src/lib/map/useMapSelect.ts) already handles Shift+click and a Shift rubber band, but only for rooms and walls, through queryRenderedFeatures on the floor plan layers.
  • Panorama pins are DOM markers rendered by MapObjectMarkers, not map features.
  • MapLibre's Shift+drag box zoom is already disabled while the Select tool is active.
  • Panorama projects are large (the Kuwait sample has 2,097 panoramas). The box test has to run over the pins' projected screen positions, not rendered-feature queries or DOM hit-testing.

Rules (PRD + PM answers on #1046)

  1. Only while Panorama Link mode is on.
  2. Shift+click on a panorama selects it. Shift+click on a pin that is already selected removes it; on another pin it adds that pin. This is the same convention rooms use today.
  3. Shift+press on the map and drag draws a selection box. Shift only has to be held when the box starts; the drag can finish without it.
  4. The box selects a panorama only when its whole marker is inside the box. The box replaces the current selection.
  5. Only panoramas on the active floor count, and hidden pins cannot be selected.
  6. Without Shift, today's behaviour is unchanged (PM): a click selects the object and opens its Information panel, and dragging a pin moves that one pin.
  7. The selection gets one outline around all of it; a single panorama gets one too. Selected pins look clearly different from unselected ones.
  8. Clicking outside the selection clears it, and the outline disappears. Clicking a selected pin, or the outline and its controls, does not clear it.
  9. The selection also clears when Panorama Link mode ends or the active floor changes.

Out of scope

  • Resize/rotate handles and any change of position (part 3).

Acceptance criteria

  • Shift+click selects, adds and removes panoramas; the outline wraps the whole selection.
  • Shift+drag draws a box, Shift can be released mid-drag, and only fully enclosed panoramas get selected.
  • Panoramas on other floors and hidden pins are never selected.
  • A plain click and a plain pin drag behave exactly as before.
  • A click outside clears the selection; a click on the selection or its outline does not.
  • Box selection stays responsive on the Kuwait sample (2,097 panoramas).
  • Unit tests for the containment rule and the active-floor / hidden filters.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; checked in the browser on a scratch copy.

RESULT

Released to development.

Shift+click adds or removes a panorama and never starts a pin drag; Shift+press on the map draws a box (Shift only needed to start it) that takes a panorama only when its whole marker is inside, and replaces the selection. One outline wraps the selection and follows the markers every frame, under the marker layer so pins stay clickable. A click outside — empty map, ghosted room, or any marker not in the selection — clears it. Only the active floor is selectable, and whatever stops being selectable drops out, which covers a floor switch and leaving the mode.

Two fixes in MapObjectMarkers make the positions trustworthy: a selection outside the viewport buffer is still projected (no button mounted) so the outline can span it, and a marker that stops being projected no longer leaves its last screen position behind — Nearby (nearbyInViewport) read those stale entries too.

Tests: src/lib/map/__tests__/panoramaSelection.test.ts, PanoramaSelectionOverlay.test.tsx, MapObjectMarkers.panoramaLink.test.tsx, plus the selection lifecycle in panoramaLinkScope.test.tsx. Mutation-checked. pnpm test / pnpm lint / tsc --noEmit green.

Browser check on the GPU: Shift+click one, box selected 27 with none outside the box, click on a selected pin keeps it, click on a ghosted room clears it, leaving the scope clears it.

Commit: 8386956 · PR #1052 -> development (1a19e47)

Demo (54 s): .playwright-mcp/demo/1049/video-1049-shift-select.mp4 — Shift+click, the Shift box with Shift released mid-drag, and a click outside clearing it. Part of the feature-wide one in .playwright-mcp/demo/1046/.

Released to main: PR #1054 (9faeb19).

issues.display_title: Issue #1050: feat(map): move, rotate, scale and reset a panorama selection as one group (#1046 part 3)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1050-group-transform.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: PRD #1046 (Panorama Link Mode Selection), part 3 of 3. Builds on #1049.

Context

  • The existing placement tools only ever write a whole frame: the project, building or level mapTransform. Nothing writes a subset of objects yet.
  • A panorama's position is its point's plan x,y on its level. Map positions convert through the level/building/project frames with lngLatToLevelPixel, the path the single-pin drag already uses (src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:261).
  • Connection lines follow automatically. They are derived from pin positions, so link data never changes.
  • Closest existing UI: the Add Panorama import alignment step (src/components/editor/add-panorama/ApplyLocationModal.tsx, #964) already has corner resize handles, a rotate handle and Reset for a rigid group of markers. It lives inside a modal rather than on the map, so it is a reference, not a drop-in.

Rules (PRD + PM answers on #1046)

  1. The selection outline carries four corner resize handles and one rotate handle, for a single panorama as well as for a group (PM).
  2. Dragging inside the outline moves the whole selection.
  3. A corner handle scales the selection about its centre. The spacing between panoramas changes; the pin markers keep their size (PM).
  4. The rotate handle rotates the selection about its centre.
  5. In this scope the transform popup's rotate / scale / nudge / reset act on the selection. With nothing selected they stay inert, as in #1048.
  6. Reset returns the selection to the positions it had when it was selected (PM). No original position is stored anywhere.
  7. The outline and its handles follow the selection during every gesture.
  8. Each gesture is one undo step. Mousemove writes only the drag preview store, and release does one setCanvasData, the same pattern as the building and wall-vertex drags (#675).
  9. It must stay responsive on the Kuwait sample (2,097 panoramas).

Out of scope

  • Selecting panoramas (#1049) and the ghost mode (#1048).
  • Moving other object types as a group.

Acceptance criteria

  • Resize and rotate handles show on the outline for one panorama and for a group.
  • Move, rotate and scale apply to every selected panorama together, and the links follow.
  • Scaling changes spacing only; marker size is unchanged.
  • The popup's rotate / scale / nudge act on the selection, and Reset puts it back where it was when selected.
  • The outline tracks the selection during gestures.
  • One undo step per gesture, and nothing is saved mid-gesture.
  • Panoramas outside the selection, other floors, buildings and frames are untouched.
  • Unit tests for the group move/rotate/scale/reset math on plan coordinates.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green; checked in the browser on a scratch copy.

RESULT

Released to development.

Corner resize handles and a rotate knob on the outline (shown for a single panorama too), on a layer above the markers so no pin label covers them. A press inside the outline — or on a pin that is in the selection — moves the whole selection; a pin outside keeps its own drag. A corner scales the spacing about the selection's centre with the markers keeping their size; the knob rotates about the same centre. The placement popup's rotate / scale / nudge / reset act on the selection in this scope, nudge stepping back through the project, building and the floor's own frame. Reset returns each panorama to where it joined the selection (panoramaSelectionOrigins). One undo step per gesture; no frame, unselected panorama or other floor is touched, and the connection lines follow because they are drawn from the points.

Judgement call for the PM: dragging a pin that is IN the selection moves the whole selection (R10/R15); a pin outside keeps the single-pin drag confirmed in Q5.

Performance. Gestures preview through usePanoramaPreviewStore (positions only), not a preview canvas: a group gesture changes points inside the level, so a preview canvas rebuilt every marker anchor and re-rendered every marker button per frame. Kuwait (Sample) scratch copy, 227 panoramas selected, dev build on the GPU: 3 fps / worst frame 1167 ms, against 29 fps for a plain pan. After: 19 fps / worst frame 83 ms, commit to paint 928 ms -> 108 ms. Still one-off expensive: a box select of 227 pins costs ~1.5 s CPU in dev, mostly React re-rendering the 691 mounted markers.

Tests: src/lib/map/__tests__/panoramaTransform.test.ts, usePanoramaGroupGesture.test.tsx, the popup group tools in panoramaLinkScope.test.tsx, handles in PanoramaSelectionOverlay.test.tsx, pin group drag in MapObjectMarkers.panoramaLink.test.tsx. Mutation-checked. pnpm test (277 files / 2,518) / pnpm lint / tsc --noEmit green.

Browser check on the GPU: group move with unselected pins untouched, undo in one step, rotate, scale, popup nudge, Reset back to the selection's start position and spread.

Demo (all three tasks, 2 min): .playwright-mcp/demo/1046/video-1046-panorama-link.mp4

Commit: 19ef018 · PR #1053 -> development (18296e9)

Demo (95 s): .playwright-mcp/demo/1050/video-1050-group-transform.mp4 — group move, rotate, scale and Reset Placement, each asserted in the scenario.

Released to main: PR #1054 (9faeb19).

issues.display_title: Issue #1055: fix(preview): tapping a shop draws the editor's blue selection ring on its roof logo
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1055-logo-ring.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported with a screenshot (samples/image-selection.png): on the viewer, tapping a shop opens its info card and paints a blue rectangle around the shop's logo on the roof. A visitor is not editing anything — the card is the feedback; the ring is an editor affordance that leaked into the published map.

Root cause

The Closed-room logo (PRD R10/R11) is painted on the roof by MapObjectMarkers, and its selection ring rides on the image itself, because the button box stays screen-axis-aligned while the image shears with the roof:

// src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx:1073 (LinkedContent, roof-logo branch)
className={cn("max-w-none object-contain", selected && !active && "ring-2 ring-blue-500")}

selected comes straight from the selectedIds prop, and the viewer passes the current selection into it exactly like the editor does:

// src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:1187
selectedIds={selectedMarkerIds}
// :1069 — selectedMarkerIds = selection ? [selection.id] : []

PreviewOverlay is the single component behind preview mode in the editor, /preview/[projectId], /v/[key] and the embed, so all four surfaces draw it.

The same selected flag drives two more rings on the same path — both stay (see the decision below):

Marker Line Selected look This task
Roof logo (Closed room) MapObjectMarkers.tsx:1073 blue ring around the image removed in the viewer
Plate label (text/icon/logo/photo/area) MapObjectMarkers.tsx:970 blue ring around the whole label pill unchanged
Panorama chip MapObjectMarkers.tsx:1095 blue ring on the round chip unchanged

Decision (PM, 2026-09-18)

Only the image. The ring goes from the roof logo in the viewer; the plate labels and the panorama chips keep theirs, so a visitor can still see which marker the card belongs to. The logo is the one case where the ring frames a picture painted on the roof and reads as an editing handle.

Scope

  1. Drop the selection ring on the roof logo in the viewer only — preview mode, /preview, /v/:key and the embed. The editor keeps it: there, selecting a room is an edit target.
  2. MapObjectMarkers has no notion of which surface it is on — PreviewOverlay has to say so. One boolean threaded to the roof-logo branch of LinkedContent (:1073); selectedIds itself stays as it is, because the other two rings still read it.
  3. activeId is not selection and must survive — the "you are here" panorama highlight (aria-current, the beacon and the offset ring, :993/:1093) is a wayfinding state the viewer needs.
  4. Keep the hit target. The ring is cosmetic; the logo stays clickable and still opens the card (pointerEvents: "auto" on the image, #997).
  5. Hover stays as it is — this task does not touch the hover highlight.

Acceptance criteria

  • On /v/:key, /preview/:projectId and the editor's preview mode, clicking a shop with a roof logo opens the info card and draws no rectangle around the logo.
  • The same click still selects: the card shows the right shop, cross-floor select and the Direction flow are unchanged.
  • In the same viewer, selecting a plate-label marker or a panorama chip still shows its blue ring.
  • In the editor (Map view), selecting a Closed room with a logo still shows the ring on the logo.
  • The current-panorama "you are here" highlight still renders in the viewer.
  • Panorama Link mode in the editor (#1048–#1050) keeps its selection outline.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #1064: fix(preview): the share modal overflows the viewport and cannot be scrolled
issues.main_description_html:
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported in #1062 (screenshot): the Share Published Project modal is taller than the browser window. The title bar with the close button is cut off above the top edge, the embed snippet is cut off below the bottom edge, and nothing scrolls — the only way out is Escape or a click on the backdrop.

Root cause

PreviewModal — the shared shell every preview modal is built on — centres the popup on the viewport and clips whatever does not fit:

// src/components/preview/PreviewModal.tsx:58 (Dialog.Popup)
className={`fixed left-[50vw] top-1/2 z-[101] flex w-full max-w-md -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2
            flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-[14px] border p-0 ...`}

Three things add up:

  1. no max-height, so the popup grows to the height of its content;
  2. top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2, so the excess splits evenly above and below the fold;
  3. overflow-hidden, so the excess is clipped and no scrollbar appears.

The body wrapper (:103, flex flex-col gap-4 p-5) does not scroll either, so once the content is taller than the window it is simply unreachable.

Why it shows up now: the Share modal keeps growing — Secured Project (#946, only for users who can manage security), Share Link, Embed to Virtual Tour (#383) and Embed Map. On the reporter's 847 px-tall viewport that is past the window; with Secured Project hidden it still fits, which is why it was not caught earlier.

The bug is in the shell, so it belongs to every modal built on it:

Modal File
Share Published Project src/components/preview/PreviewShareModal.tsx
Manage collaborators (list grows per collaborator) src/components/collaboration/ManageCollaboratorsModal.tsx
Publish / unpublish confirm src/components/preview/PreviewConfirmDialog.tsx
Owner-only notice src/components/collaboration/OwnerOnlyDialog.tsx

Scope

  1. Cap the popup at the viewport — max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] on Dialog.Popup, so it can never extend past the fold. dvh, not vh, because of the collapsing browser chrome on mobile.
  2. Scroll the body, not the popup — min-h-0 overflow-y-auto on the content wrapper (:103), so the header (title + close button) and the footer (action buttons) stay pinned and reachable while the middle scrolls.
  3. Fix the shell, not the Share modal — all four consumers above are the same defect; patching PreviewShareModal alone leaves ManageCollaboratorsModal broken for a long collaborator list.
  4. No visual change when the content fits — short modals (OwnerOnlyDialog, PreviewConfirmDialog) must render exactly as they do today; the cap and the scroll only engage when the content is taller than the window.

Acceptance criteria

  • At 1600×847 with Secured Project visible, the Share modal fits inside the viewport: the title bar and close button are visible, and the embed snippet is reachable by scrolling inside the modal.
  • Nothing is clipped above or below the viewport at any window height.
  • The header and footer stay in place while the body scrolls.
  • Modals shorter than the viewport look unchanged.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Source: #1062

RESULT

Fixed in the shared shell src/components/preview/PreviewModal.tsx, so the share modal, the collaborator list, the publish/unpublish confirmations and the owner-only notice are all covered:

  • max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] on Dialog.Popup — dvh, not vh, for collapsing mobile browser chrome.
  • min-h-0 overflow-y-auto on the body wrapper — min-h-0 is what lets a flex child shrink below its content; without it the cap pushes the overflow back outside the popup instead of scrolling it.
  • shrink-0 on the header and the footer, so the title bar and the action buttons stay pinned while the body scrolls.

Measured on the dashboard → … → Share of a published, secured project at 1600×847:

before after
dialog top y = -104.6 y = 16
dialog height 1056 (viewport 847) 815
clipped above / below true / true false / false
body overflow-y visible auto (scrollHeight 982 > clientHeight 743)

Screenshots: .playwright-mcp/screenshot/1064-share-{before,after,after-scrolled}.png; the scrolled one shows the full <iframe> snippet reachable with the title bar still in place.

Guard tests in src/components/preview/__tests__/PreviewModal.test.tsx (the cap, the body being what scrolls, the header/footer out of that scroll) — jsdom has no layout, so they assert the box rules; mutation-checked by reverting all four classes, all three go red.

pnpm test 278 files / 2523 passed + 3 skipped · tsc --noEmit 0 · pnpm lint clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #1061: fix(editor): setting a floor image rescales the floor, moving the building and stranding its markers
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1061-floor-image.mp4

Source report: #1056 (video by QA).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Setting a floor plan image on a floor that already has geometry moves that floor on the map and leaves its markers behind. In the report's video (Square One Mall V6 demo, production): after picking an image in Edit Floor, the 2D canvas shows the plan shrunk into the top-left corner while the access icons stay spread out, and on the Map tab the floor's markers have jumped about a kilometre to the Highway 403 interchange while the other floor is still on the mall.

Root cause

Loading a backdrop rescales the floor's geometry into the image's pixel space:

// src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:360 (setBackdrop)
if (adoptBackdropSize(ctx)) { fit2D(ctx); recomputeRooms(ctx, false); emitScale(ctx); notifyChange(ctx); }
// src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts:110
export function scaleModelToSize(model: Model, iw: number, ih: number): boolean {
  if (!iw || !ih || (model.w === iw && model.h === ih)) return false;
  const s = Math.max(iw, ih) / Math.max(model.w, model.h);
  for (const o of [...model.walls, ...model.doors, ...(model.windows || []), ...model.icons]) { /* × s */ }
  for (const rn of model.roomNames || []) { rn.x *= s; rn.y *= s; }
  for (const ma of model.manualAreas || []) ma.points = ma.points.map(([x, y]) => [x * s, y * s]);
  model.w = iw; model.h = ih;
  return true;
}

Two separate defects come out of that:

  1. Half the floor is rescaled. Model also carries points, safety, access and shapes (floorplan/types.ts:65-68), and modelToLevel writes them straight back (bridge.ts:388-411). None of them are scaled here, and level.panoramas never enters the model at all. So walls and areas move into the new pixel space while every marker stays in the old one.
  2. The scale is about the origin (0, 0), but the map projects through one document-wide coordSpace anchored at the old bbox centre. reprojectLevels(written, [id]) keeps that space for a multi-floor placed project (only a whole-document re-projection may re-derive it, geojson-utils.ts:412), so the rescaled floor slides and changes size on the map. On a project with no placement the coord space is re-derived instead — and then the other floors move.

The behaviour also contradicts the ruling this modal documents:

// src/components/editor/EditLevelModal.tsx:118
// The image is a TRACING BACKDROP, nothing more. Existing geometry lives in
// canvasData.levels and is never rescaled or re-scanned when the raster under
// it changes (#878 ruling 2)

adoptBackdropSize exists for scan results, whose coordinates are already image pixels — i.e. for a floor that has no geometry of its own yet.

Measured (unit probe, toy model with a 50 m footprint, saved-document state: pinned + frozen coord space)

Case Walls move Markers move Wall↔marker gap
Placed project, image larger than the plan 10.1 m 0 m 30.5 m → 20.6 m
Placed project, image smaller than the plan 7.1 m 0 m 30.5 m → 37.5 m
Unplaced project, image smaller 0.7 m 3.2 m + the sibling floor moves 6.0 m

The displacement is proportional to the project's footprint, so a 400 m mall gives the hundreds-of-metres jump in the video.

Scope

  1. A floor that already has geometry must not be rescaled when a backdrop image loads. The image is a tracing backdrop: fit the image to the plan, not the plan to the image.
  2. Keep the scan path working. A floor whose geometry comes from /v1/predict is in image-pixel coordinates already; that path (bridge.ts:438, the upload/reset path in FloorplanEditor.tsx:725) must be unaffected.
  3. A floor already traced against its own image stays a no-op — model.w/h already equals the image size, so scaleModelToSize returns false today and must keep doing so.
  4. Where a rescale legitimately happens, it must cover the whole floor — points, safety, access and shapes as well as walls, areas and openings.
  5. No migration. Projects already corrupted by this are out of scope; this stops the corruption from happening again.

Acceptance criteria

  • Setting, changing or removing a floor plan image on a floor that has geometry leaves every wall, area, pin, safety annotation, access point, shape and panorama exactly where it was — in the editor canvas, in the Map tab and in the viewer.
  • The building's position, rotation and size on the map are unchanged by setting a floor image, on a placed project and on an unplaced one.
  • Setting an image on one floor does not move any other floor.
  • The image renders under the plan as a backdrop, with the opacity slider still working.
  • A new floor created from a scanned image still lines up with that image.
  • Repeating the report's steps on the demo project no longer moves the building (#1056).
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

The image is now fitted to the plan instead of the plan to the image.

  • floorplan/geometry.ts — new backdropFit (letterbox the image into the plan's box, anchored at (0, 0)); scaleModelToSize also carries points, safety, access and shapes
  • editor/model-sync.ts — adoptBackdropSize only acts on an empty floor
  • editor/draw.ts — the backdrop is drawn at its fitted rect, not stretched to the plan box

A/B on two identical scratch copies, opening the floor whose image no longer matches its plan: on development the stored plan size goes 1242×521 → 400×240 and the building moves (map SSIM 0.9858, and it auto-saves that); on the fix every number is unchanged and the map is pixel-identical (SSIM 1.000). New backdrop-rebase.test.ts fails if the guard is removed. pnpm test 278 files / 2532 passed, pnpm lint and pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Side effect worth having: opening a project whose floors are still in a scan grid no longer silently rewrites their geometry and auto-saves it.

issues.display_title: Issue #1071: fix(preview): the information card never appears in embed mode
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1071-embed-info.mp4

Source report: #1070 (video by QA).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Embedding the map in an ordinary website and tapping a shop selects the marker but shows nothing: the information card never appears. In the report's video the embed runs inside the W3Schools TryIt editor (<iframe src="https://map-thru.com/embed/UkZnTKwv" …>); markers ring, the Event panel opens and "View The District Kitchen" flies the camera — but no information is ever displayed.

Reproduced on production, same click on both surfaces:

Route Clicked Information card
/v/UkZnTKwv Walmart, linked to McDonald's (inside Walmart) shown — title + description
/embed/UkZnTKwv the same marker nothing rendered

Root cause

// src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:159
const framed = embedded || tourFramed;
const infoCardHidden = framed;
…
// :1388
{detail && !infoCardHidden && ( /* the information card */ )}

/embed/[key] was built for one consumer (#315): a GoThru virtual tour iframing the map, where the tour owns information display, so the card is suppressed. /v/[key] already makes that conditional — tourFramed only goes true when document.referrer is on the GoThru tour allowlist (isGothruTourReferrer, src/lib/preview/tourBridge.ts). /embed/[key] suppresses it unconditionally, so every embed on a normal website loses the card with nothing to replace it.

Decision (PM, 2026-09-18)

Follow the /v rule. The card shows in an embed like it does on the live view, and is hidden only when the parent really is a GoThru tour.

Scope

  1. Split the two facts framed currently carries. The small pane a framed viewer gets (compact panels, #770 R41) stays tied to embedded; who owns information display becomes the tour test alone — infoCardHidden follows tourFramed, not embedded.
  2. Detect the tour by more than the referrer. A tour that sets referrerpolicy="no-referrer" (or any browser that strips it) would otherwise show two copies of the information. Treat an inbound PANO_CHANGE from an allowed origin (GOTHRU_TOUR_ORIGINS, already parsed by useTourSync/tourBridge) as proof the parent is a tour and hide the card from that point on.
  3. Nothing else about the embed changes — the toolbar, Event panel, Direction flow, panorama chips, the tour postMessage bridge and the compact panel sizing stay exactly as they are.
  4. The editor and /preview are untouched: they never set embedded.

Acceptance criteria

  • In an <iframe src="/embed/:key"> on an ordinary website, tapping a marker opens the information card, with the same content as /v/:key.
  • Inside a GoThru tour (referrer on the allowlist) an /embed/:key iframe still shows no card.
  • A tour that sends PANO_CHANGE with no referrer also ends up with no card once the message arrives.
  • /v/:key is unchanged on both sides of that test.
  • Panels in an embed keep their compact sizing, and the toolbar/Event/Direction flows are unchanged.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

infoCardHidden now follows the tour test alone; the compact panel sizing stays tied to embedded.

// src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx
const framed = embedded || tourFramed;   // small pane: any iframe
const infoCardHidden = tourFramed;       // the tour, and only the tour, owns info display

tourFramed = tourReferrer || tourConnected. The new tourConnected comes from useTourSync: true once a PANO_CHANGE has arrived from an allowed GoThru origin, so a tour with referrerpolicy="no-referrer" still hides the card instead of showing the information twice. It is a second listener on the existing (multiplexing) bridge — createTourSync is untouched.

Verified on the published Square One map, clicking Walmart, linked to McDonald's (inside Walmart): production rendered no panel before the release and opens the same card as /v/:key after it. Tests: PreviewOverlay.embedInfoCard.test.tsx (5 cases) and useTourSync.tourConnected.test.tsx (4 cases); reverting infoCardHidden to framed turns two red. pnpm test 281 files / 2544 passed, pnpm lint and pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean. Demo: .playwright-mcp/demo/1071/video-1071-embed-info.mp4.

issues.display_title: Issue #1072: fix(editor): the loading overlay never clears when returning from the preview
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1072-preview-back.mp4

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported in #1067 (80 s screen recording): open a project in the editor, hit Preview, then Back to Editor — the editor never arrives. It sits on the loading overlay's last phase, "Preparing editor…", for as long as the recording runs (the reporter's stopwatch passes 1:30). Only a reload gets out of it.

The editor underneath has in fact finished loading: the canvas is drawn, the floor list and the 48 objects of the sidebar are populated. It is the overlay that never leaves — and it is fixed inset-0 z-[200] with a solid background and pointer-events, so the working editor is unreachable behind it.

Reproduced locally at /editor/6397e363-… → Preview → Back to Editor: cold open clears in 6.4 s, the round trip never clears (stopped at 45 s).

Root cause

Two rules that are each correct on their own, deadlocking when they meet — the loading overlay (#1028) against the warm-store hydrate guard that predates it.

  1. src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts:134 — every restore declares a build phase before hydrating, unconditionally:
const enterBuildPhase = async () => {
  const loading = useEditorLoadingStore.getState();
  flushSync(() => {
    loading.setCanvasReady(false);   // "a model build is pending"
    loading.setDataReady(true);
  });
  await nextPaint();
};
  1. src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:185 — hydratePersistedState skips the whole restore when the store is already warm for this project, which is exactly what an editor ↔ preview SPA hop leaves behind:
if (projectId && store.projectId === projectId && store.canvasData?.levels?.length) return;

So the hop declares a build and then builds nothing. canvasReady is left false, and the effect that would set it back to true (src/components/editor/FloorplanEditor.tsx:623) only re-runs on [canvasData, activeId, floorConfigs, engineReady] — a skipped hydrate writes none of them, so it never runs again and nothing clears the phase.

Instrumented store log for the hop (temporary, reverted):

34564  EFFECT engineReady=true ref===activeId  → canvasReady=true
36075  canvasReady=false   ← enterBuildPhase
36076  dataReady=true
36220  projectReady=true
       (no further EFFECT — ever)

Mutation check: with the guard at wizardState.ts:185 disabled the overlay never appears on the hop at all; restored, it hangs again.

The same trap is behind the other two skip paths, so the fix must cover them, not just the preview hop:

Skip Line When
warm store, same project wizardState.ts:185 editor ↔ preview navigation
hasUnsavedChanges || isSaving wizardState.ts:178 opening the editor while an autosave PUT is in flight
restoreFromLocal with no session / no blob useWizardPersistence.ts:99 fall-through path when the server has no floorplan

Scope

  1. Only declare a build that will actually happen. hydratePersistedState should report whether it applied the snapshot, and the caller should clear the build phase (setCanvasReady(true)) when it did not — there is nothing to wait for.
  2. One source of truth. Do not re-implement the skip conditions inside useWizardPersistence; duplicating them means the next skip rule added to the hydrate silently hangs the editor again.
  3. Cover the restoreFromLocal path too — it can also write nothing at all.
  4. No change to the guard itself. The warm-store and in-flight-save skips exist to stop a stale blob rolling back the store (editor → preview save race); they stay.
  5. No change to the cold-open behaviour: the overlay must still cover the whole load, including the synchronous model build, on a reload or a project switch.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor → Preview → Back to Editor lands in a usable editor, with the overlay gone.
  • The same round trip repeated three times in a row still clears every time.
  • A cold open (reload / project switch) still shows "Loading project…" → "Loading floor plan…" → "Preparing editor…" and clears when the canvas is on screen.
  • Opening the editor while an autosave is in flight does not pin the overlay.
  • A guard test fails if the build phase is declared for a hydrate that is skipped.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

Source: #1067

RESULT

Fixed in src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts + src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts (commit 0882ac2, PR #1076 → development 3c28a10).

hydratePersistedState now reports whether it applied the snapshot, and the restore settles the build phase itself when no build is coming:

const settleBuildPhase = (applied: boolean) => {
  const levels = useMapStore.getState().canvasData?.levels.length ?? 0;
  if (!applied || levels === 0) useEditorLoadingStore.getState().setCanvasReady(true);
};

One predicate, at the place that knows the answer, covering all three ways a restore can build nothing: skipped as stale (warm store on the editor ↔ preview hop, unsaved edits, a save in flight), the fall-through restoreFromLocal with no session or no blob, and a project with no level at all. restoreFromLocal reports the same way. The guard at wizardState.ts:185 is untouched.

Verified in Chrome on the reporter's path:

before (development) after
editor → Preview → Back to Editor stuck on "Preparing editor…", stopped at 45 s clears every time, 3 rounds
leaving the preview mid-load — clears, 3 rounds
cold open Loading project… → Loading floor plan… → clear 6.1 s unchanged, 6.2 s

Screenshots 1072-preview-back-before.png / -after.png; demo .playwright-mcp/demo/1072/video-1072-preview-back.mp4 (both halves in one take on a scratch copy — the take fails if the "before" build ever clears).

Guards in src/hooks/__tests__/useWizardPersistence.loadingPhase.test.tsx: the three restores that build nothing settle the phase, and a restore that really does build keeps it up. Mutation-checked — reverting the fix turns the first three red.

pnpm test 280 files / 2539 passed + 3 skipped · tsc --noEmit 0 · pnpm lint clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #1075: fix(preview): the Share modal never confirms that a project password is set
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-1075-password-set.mp4

Source report: #1063 (screenshot by QA).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

QA sets a project password in the Share Published Project modal and reports it is not saved. It is saved. Verified end to end on a scratch copy against the production API — set, changed, and cleared — with a stranger's browser answering the gate at /v/<key>:

Step Result
Secure a published project with a password switch still true after a reload; /v/<key> shows the locked gate
Enter that password as a visitor unlocked, map loads
Type a new password over the (blank) field and save Saved
Try the old password That password is not correct. Try again.
Try the new password unlocked
Turn the switch off and save /v/<key> opens with no gate

The backend is not involved: update.go hashes the plaintext into password_hash and unlock.go checks it with bcrypt, both correct.

Root cause — the UI never says a password is in place

The password is write-only by design (#946): the API hashes it and never sends it back, so there is nothing to prefill the input with. What is missing is any other evidence that the project currently has one.

// src/components/preview/SecuredProjectSection.tsx:41-42
const needsPassword = enabled && !alreadySecured && password.trim().length === 0;
const dirty = enabled !== alreadySecured || password.length > 0;   // false at rest

Re-opening the modal on an already-secured project therefore shows an empty field and a greyed-out Save security button — exactly the screenshot in the report. The only hint that a password exists is the input's placeholder, "Leave blank to keep the current one", which reads just as easily as "there is nothing here".

The success feedback is also gone by the time anyone looks:

// :66-67
setSave("saved");
window.setTimeout(() => setSave("idle"), 2000);   // green "Saved" lasts 2s

Scope

  1. State the fact, don't imply it. visibility === "secured" already is "a password is set" — the API refuses a secured project without one (update.go:153), so no new field and no API change is needed. Show it: a status line on an already-secured project saying a password is set and that typing a new one replaces it.
  2. Keep the confirmation on screen. Drop the 2 s revert; the Saved state stays until the next edit (typing, or flipping the switch) clears it.
  3. Nothing else changes — the write-only contract, the gate, the embed grant, and the off/on behaviour all stay exactly as they are.

Acceptance criteria

  • Opening the Share modal on a secured project states that a password is set, without revealing it.
  • After saving, the confirmation stays visible until the next edit instead of vanishing after 2 s.
  • A password can still be set, changed and removed; the field stays empty and write-only.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Merged into development as 9e787af (PR #1078), commit be873c4.

The password was always being saved — proven end to end on a scratch copy against the production API, with a stranger's browser answering the gate at /v/<key>: setting it locks the project, the current password unlocks it, a changed password takes effect (the old one is refused), and turning security off removes the gate. update.go and unlock.go were never at fault.

What was broken is that nothing in the modal said a password was in place. src/components/preview/SecuredProjectSection.tsx:

  • a status line on an already-secured project — "A password is set — type a new one to replace it, or leave the field blank to keep it." No new API field: visibility === "secured" already is "a password is set", because the API refuses a secured project without one (update.go:153);
  • the placeholder now describes the field (New password) instead of the state;
  • dropped window.setTimeout(() => setSave("idle"), 2000) — the Saved confirmation stays until the next edit clears it.

The write-only contract is untouched: the field is still never prefilled, a blank field still means "keep the current one", and the gate, the embed grant and the off/on behaviour are unchanged.

60 fps before/after demo (.playwright-mcp/demo/1075/), same steps on development (:6060) and the fix (:6070), one published and already-secured scratch project:

status line placeholder button 5 s after saving
BEFORE 0 Leave blank to keep the current one Save security
AFTER 1 New password Saved

Two new tests in src/components/preview/__tests__/SecuredProjectSection.test.tsx, both mutation-checked. pnpm test 2546 passed · pnpm lint clean · tsc --noEmit clean. The scratch copy was deleted afterwards.

Released — PR #1079 merged development → main as 3b60e62; deploy run 35326332022 completed success at 2026-09-18T08:51:17Z. The Share modal is behind a login, so it was not exercised on production directly; the public routes were smoke-checked after the release (map-thru.com/ and /login 200, and /embed/UkZnTKwv still returns the information card — 1 panel).
